Read a JSON Web Key

Source: R/keys.R
as_jwk.Rd

as_jwk() reads a JWK (RFC 7517) from its JSON text or from a list already parsed. A raw vector is taken as an oct secret, as by jwk_oct().

Usage

as_jwk(x, ...)

Arguments

x

JWK text, a parsed JWK as a named list, a raw secret, or a jwk.

...

Not used.

Value

A jwk.

Details

RSA keys need n and e, and for a private key all of d, p, q, dp, dq and qi; they are checked when read. A PEM string holding an RSA key, in PKCS#1, PKCS#8 or SubjectPublicKeyInfo, is read too.

EC keys on P-256, P-384 and P-521 and OKP keys on X25519 are checked when read: the point must be on its curve. PEM holding an EC or X25519 key is read too. Other OKP keys, such as Ed25519, are read and kept so that they can be listed, selected and thumbprinted, but cannot be used.

Secrets in memory

zujose is pure R, and so are its keys: an oct secret, and the private members of an RSA, EC or X25519 key, are ordinary R vectors. R copies vectors freely and has no way to wipe one, so a secret may stay in memory after the key is gone, and may reach a saved workspace or a core dump. zujose never prints secret members and never puts them in an error message, but it cannot do more than that. Keep long-lived secrets out of saved workspaces (.RData) and load them from a secret store when they are needed.

Examples

key <- as_jwk(
  '{"kty":"oct","kid":"k1","alg":"HS256","k":"hJtXIZ2uSN5kbQfbtTNWbpdmhkV8FJG-Onbc6mxCcYg"}'
)
key
#> <jwk> oct, 256 bits
#>   kid "k1"
#>   alg HS256
#>   private: yes (not shown)
